subject: Bridge incentive request — embedding latency regression impacting Acme PDM
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.co>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Increased embedding latency impacting PDM feature

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing a significant degradation in embedding latency beginning late last night (Apr 19, ~23:45 PDT). Average embedding response time for our PDM search calls has jumped from ~30ms to ~500-800ms and we've observed ~12% request timeouts downstream (frontend returning 504). This is blocking our phased launch of the new similarity-ranking flow.

Can your team confirm:
- Whether there was a rollout or config change overnight that could explain this?
- ETA for a fix or a rollback?
- What remediation / financial make-whole you can provide while this is impacting our launch schedule?

We can share logs and request traces from our side (attached minimal traces in this initial message). This is high priority for us — the product manager is pushing to pause the rollout if we can't stabilize within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Product Integrations
Acme Robotics

[attachment: acme_latency_logs.txt]

- I'll open a formal incident and I expect we can either rollback or push a targeted fix within 48 hours; I will confirm within 2 hours after product triage.
- For remediation, I want to propose a provisional goodwill credit while we investigate — we can propose a formal amount once we understand scope, but I want to signal we're willing to compensate for the launch impact.

Next steps: Kar (cc) — can you take lead on root cause triage and advise on rollback vs patch? Marissa (cc) — FYI on potential credit ask; I'll follow up with a proposed amount and need for finance approval.

Samantha — can you share approximate API volume for embeddings over the last 24 hours and any SLA impacts you are tracking (e.g., revenue/cancelations tied to the rollout)? That will help size the recommendation.

Again — apologies and thanks for the patience. I'll update within the hour.

Best,

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Acme embedding latency — ask for product timeline + provisional credit approval

Team — summarizing customer impact and asking for approvals:

What happened: Acme reporting embedding latency spike ~Apr 19 23:45 PDT. Their PDM similarity search is timing out; launch of new feature is at risk within 48 hours.

Requested from Product (Karthik):
- Root cause determination and recon of whether last-night rollout included a kernel/quantization change for embedding models.
- ETA for rollback or targeted patch.

Finance/RevOps (Marissa):
- Acme is asking for make-whole. Proposed commercial options for exec approval: (A) one-time invoice credit of $18k (approx. 2 weeks of expected embedding spend) or (B) 30% discount on embeddings bill for the next 2 billing cycles. Both paired with a written SLA remediation plan.

Why this ask: Acme is a mid-enterprise PLG expansion; the delayed launch materially impacts their go-to-market timeline and upsell trajectory. We should be constructive but keep the ask conditional on product commitment and a short-term commercial step.

Attachments: acme_latency_logs.txt (sent by customer).

Target decision timeline: need provisional approval (yes/no) to offer to Acme within 6 business hours so they don't pause launch. If we need exec signature, please flag immediately.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Acme embedding latency — ask for product timeline + provisional credit approval

Quick technical summary after triage:
- Root cause: a rollout of a quantization kernel variant for our embeddings runtime was promoted to canary last night. The new kernel has a codepath-opt that increases per-sequence micro-ops for short sequences, which regresses tail latency on low-length inputs (exactly what Acme is sending).
- Impact: higher p50->p95, and increased 504s under steady load. Not a hardware issue.

Mitigation plan:
- Short term (next 0-48 hours): revert to previous kernel for the affected embedding model family in the region serving Acme. This is low-risk and should restore prior latency distribution.
- Medium term: add a per-model performance gate to prevent this kernel variant from progressing to production without synthetic short-sequence benchmarks.

Commercial ask: we recommend offering a goodwill package that balances customer retention and precedents. My suggested commercial offer (product + finance alignment):
- One-time goodwill credit equal to 15% of last 2 months embedding invoiced amount (estimate to be validated) + priority scheduling for the rollback and post-mortem.

I think Kar + Marissa should finalize numeric amount; I prefer the percentage approach to avoid arbitrary fixed dollar precedents. If finance pushes for a cap, a $20k cap seems reasonable.

I will target the rollback within 24 hours; please confirm we can tell Acme "48 hours or less."

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

If product can commit to rollback within 24-48 hours, I'm comfortable approving the $20k maximum credit now pending the signed addendum.

1) Product remediation: our runtime team will rollback the new embedding quantization kernel for your serving region. Karthik has targeted a rollback and verification window within 24-48 hours from now. We will keep you updated on the incident ticket: INC-20270420-embed-latency.

2) Goodwill credit: pending your sign-off on a short addendum, we can offer a one-time goodwill credit of $20,000 applied to your next invoice (this is the cap approved by finance). If you are open to a 12-month committed renewal, we can expand the credit to $30,000 — we can discuss details separately.

3) Ask of you: please confirm acceptance of the $20k provisional credit and whether you want the credit tied to a signed addendum or prefer a quick email acknowledgement for now. Also please confirm any immediate business impact numbers (loss of revenue, paused orders) so we can track post-mortem impact analysis.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority and I will personally run weekly touchpoints until we close the post-mortem.

Best,
